svg.text: (a) Drive train from above (Rev C2 model)
the deck to the hinge shaft
(b) Side view: stage 1 along the deck, stage 2 down
Plate P13 holds the intermediate shaft
Climbing onto the first step needs the most torque, so both belt tensions peak.
Stage 1 pulls the intermediate shaft towards its motor; stage 2 pulls the hinge
shaft up towards the intermediate shaft. Acrylic and PETG parts give way to both.
(c) Hinge shaft P20 under load (one per side)
Grey: axis at rest; red: under load
Track drive pulleys (rear + front segment), outboard in the side-plate bearings
Pulley tilts, so the belt runs
out of line: slips, skips teeth
Why the left side fails first
The longer left belt has more free span, so the shafts can move further before
it pulls taut; the longer left shaft bends (91.6 / 86.6)³ = 1.18× as much.
Renders and side view from the Rev C2 CAD model; red overlays are schematic, angles exaggerated
